provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program works directly on the visible grid. It groups the non-background pixels by colour. For each colour with at least two pixels, it finds the shortest closed tour over those corners with a Held-Karp bitmask DP; two corners give a single segment. It then draws only the tour edges that are horizontal, vertical or exactly 45 degrees. A single-pixel colour that 8-touches a corner of a multi-pixel colour is a companion. It copies that colour's drawn edge cells, shifted by its own offset from the touched corner, and paints only background cells. Every part of this is invariant under D4: Euclidean tour length, the legality of an edge, and the 8-neighbour offsets all map consistently under rotation and reflection. So no axis or direction needs rewriting, and d4 needs no special constants. The palette sets two constants. BG is palette[0], the background. RANK maps each visible colour back to its original colour index. Outlines and then companions are painted in ascending original-colour order, as the generator does, so overlapping companion copies resolve the same way under any palette.
draft_notes.limitations: Nothing has been run or tested. If a companion pixel touched corners of more than one figure, it would keep the last neighbour in row-major scan order, like the archived solver. The generator's construction rules this out, but that choice is not D4-equivariant. Tied shortest tours would be broken by sorted-coordinate order. The generator guarantees a unique shortest tour, with a 1e-9 margin, for colours with three or more corners. The program assumes the background is exactly palette[0]. I found no contradictions between the fixtures and the rule.
